newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek depos, swaps softer, liquidity improving.
newsitem.headline: Greek depos, swaps softer, liquidity improving.

text.p: Short-term money rates were trading a touch softer with overnight funds down about 50 basis points from Tuesday's levels and swaps tracking depos, about 30 basis points lower across the board.

Liquidity will be helped by the renewal of a portion of maturing T-bills -- those issued in physical paper form. Maturing T-bills on December 18 in dematerialised, book-entry form will not be renewed and funds will stay in the system.
Dealers said around 200 billion drachmas were maturing and the Bank of Greece was likely to revert back to its overnight 12.40 percent bid.
On Tuesday, Greece's central bank announced that it was cutting its discount and overdraft rates by 100 basis points, down to 16.5 and 25 percent respectively.
Also, effectivE January 1 it will lower the rate it pays commercial banks on interest-bearing reserves by 150 basis points to 11 percent.
The Bank of Greece also switched its overnight intervention to the offer side injecting liquidity at 13.40 percent.
"The drop in the rate the central bank pays interest bearing reserves renders forex more expensive and thus pushes swap bids lower," said a money dealer at a state bank.
The mark was quoted at 158.25/30 drachmas from Tuesday's 158.185 fix, the dollar at 245.32/42 drachmas from 244.500 and the Ecu at 304.76/86 from 304.760 drachmas.
